summary: WebGL renderer for large graphs, with the graphology ecosystem. MIT, active, 110 KB gzip, 6.9 MB and 10 packages. No provenance, and it needs WebGL2 and browser globals at import, so use it only in client components.
reasoning: MIT and a public repository; 4.0.4 published 2026-10-27 with 14 releases in 90 days.
WebGL rendering handles graphs far larger than a canvas renderer.
110 KB gzip with graphology; 6.9 MB install and 10 packages.
No OSV advisories for 4.0.4 or graphology 0.26.0.
React integration is available via @react-sigma/core 6.0.0 (MIT, active, peers sigma ^4 and graphology ^0.26).
caveats: No npm provenance and no publish workflow; releases are manual.
Importing sigma in Node fails with 'WebGL2RenderingContext is not defined'. It must be dynamically imported or used in a client component.
No built-in layouts: pair it with graphology-layout-forceatlas2 or another layout package.
The React wrapper is a separate package with its own release cadence.
